the-handle-is-the-id-after-all.why: THE UUID WEARING THE HANDLE'S CLOTHES — the one wrong answer that looks exactly like the right one in a table. Every structural assertion still passes: the state is `RECORDED`, the field is populated, the key set is unchanged, the column is not empty. What has happened is that the register went back to naming records by an identifier no person can recognise, which is the whole of what owner decision 44 exists to end. `retention-disposal.e2e-spec.ts` fails 1 of 15, on the VALUE assertion rather than on the absence one beside it: `expected '5b95a176-993c-…' to be 'E2E-PAYREF-…'`, which is the better failure because it names the uuid against the reference that should have been there. **AND THE `why` FIRST WRITTEN HERE WAS WRONG IN EXACTLY THE WAY BATCH FOUR'S WAS, which is recorded rather than quietly corrected.** It claimed `retention-disposal.spec.ts` dies too. MEASURED, IT DOES NOT — Playwright stayed 22/22 with this plant live, because it MOCKS the register endpoint and so the api's resolver is not in its path at all. That is the finding and not a gap: a mocked endpoint supplies whatever the screen reads, so no Playwright assertion can ever catch the api resolving a handle wrongly, and the api e2e is the only layer that can.

a-destroyed-record-reads-as-sloppy-bookk.why: THE MISSING KEY COLLAPSED INTO THE NULL VALUE, which is why the repository returns a Map at all. With the `has` check gone, `handles.get()` yields `undefined` for a record that no longer exists, `?? null` turns it into `null`, and the register reports NOT_RECORDED — *this kind of record carries a reference and this one has none*. That is a FALSE statement about the office's own bookkeeping: nobody failed to write a reference down, the record itself is gone, and those are different answers to a regulator asking what was extended. It is also the milder of the two, which is the direction that does not get investigated. `retention-resolution.config.spec.ts` fails on the RECORD_NO_LONGER_PRESENT test and on nothing else — the four states are proven in a pure function precisely because no fixture can destroy a record out from under a surviving extension row.

the-three-absences-become-one-sentence.why: TWO DIFFERENT ANSWERS RENDERED AS ONE SENTENCE. The api still distinguishes them and the screen stops: a settlement, which no record of its kind can ever name, now reads *no reference recorded* — exactly as if somebody had simply not written one down. The difference is whether anybody can ever close the gap, and a register that reports an unclosable limit as an open task sends an officer looking for a reference that does not exist. `retention-disposal.spec.ts` fails 1 of 22, on the WHICH-of-the-reasons test. **CORRECTED FROM THE RUN: it dies on the POSITIVE assertion, not on the `not.toContainText` one this `why` first named.** The settlement row renders the wrong sentence, so the positive check for *No reference exists for this kind* fails before the negative is reached — and the received text in the failure is the whole row, which is a more legible report than an absence. The negatives are still worth keeping, and the honest reason is narrower than first written: with one expected sentence PER ROW a collapse always makes one positive wrong, so what the negatives add is cover for a single string that contains BOTH sentences, which no positive check would catch.

the-settlement-reason-becomes-a-shrug.from: 'a settlement carries no reference of its own, and the one hop that exists resolves to nothing: `claimId` is `@unique`, and `Claim.claimNumber` is optional at its own boundary and absent on every settlement in the e2e database (18 of 18, measured 2026-10-23). Giving one a reference means generating one, and nothing in this product generates a reference for anything — owner decision 44 forbids inventing the first scheme here.',
the-settlement-reason-becomes-a-shrug.why: THE MEASUREMENT REPLACED BY A SHRUG. `not available for this record type` is true, says nothing, and is indistinguishable from *nobody got round to it* — so the next reader adds a reference column to `Settlement` without knowing that the hop already exists (`claimId` is `@unique`), that it resolves to nothing because `Claim.claimNumber` is optional at its own boundary, or that nothing in this product generates a reference for anything. The reason field is the only place that measurement survives at runtime, which is why the spec asserts its CONTENT rather than that it is non-empty. `retention-resolution.config.spec.ts` fails on the CATEGORY_HAS_NO_REFERENCE test (`toContain('claimNumber')`) AND on the reason-length floor in the every-resolution test — two assertions, both about the same field, which is the point of having both: one catches a reword and the other catches an emptying.
